page: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processors. It features 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 2.67 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and does not include any GPUs. Network connectivity is a key feature, delivering a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 67384.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 50868.09, placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. Memory read bandwidth is also highly competitive, reaching 3741.32 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 212.97 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is average, as indicated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1458.4. Large block memory write speeds and static web serving throughput also fall into the average tier.

The server presents clear tradeoffs. While it excels at multi-threaded processing and high-throughput network operations, it exhibits poor performance in LLM text generation, with the 7B model achieving only 6.09 tokens per second. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, though the 100 Gbps network bandwidth mitigates potential bottlenecks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal allocation provides raw hardware access without hypervisor overhead, making it a viable option for network-intensive workloads, database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
